record.paper_title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Global-in-time existence of strong Navier–Stokes solutions
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations under suitable boundary conditions, do strong solutions exist globally in time?

evidence.quote: It may be superfluous to recall that it is not known whether weak solutions are unique and whether strong solutions are global in time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be either all of $\mathbb{R}^3$, the three-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^3$, or a smooth bounded domain (in the latter case, equipped with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$). Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations for the velocity field $u : [0,\infty) 	imes \Omega 	o \mathbb{R}^3$ and pressure $p : [0,\infty) 	imes \Omega 	o \mathbb{R}$:

$$\partial_t u - 
u \Delta u + (u \cdot 
abla) u + 
abla p = 0, \qquad 
abla \cdot u = 0,$$

with viscosity $
u > 0$ and smooth, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ (satisfying the boundary condition in the bounded-domain case, and decaying suitably at infinity in the case $\Omega = \mathbb{R}^3$).

A strong solution on the time interval $[0,T]$ is a solution $u$ with $u \in L^\infty(0,T; H^1(\Omega)) \cap L^2(0,T; H^2(\Omega))$ (equivalently, having the regularity necessary to be unique and to satisfy the equations in the classical sense for $t > 0$).

Question: For every smooth, divergence-free initial datum $u_0$ as above, does there exist a strong solution $u$ defined globally in time, i.e., on $[0,\infty) 	imes \Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The global-in-time existence of strong (smooth) solutions to the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations is a long-standing open problem and is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems. It remains unsolved as of 2026; only local-in-time strong solutions, global weak (Leray–Hopf) solutions, and conditional regularity results are known.

status_evidence.snippet: Waves follow our boat as we meander across the lake... Mathematicians and physicists believe that an explanation for and the prediction of both the breeze and the turbulence can be found through an understanding of solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations.
status_evidence.claim: The global existence and smoothness of 3D Navier–Stokes solutions is an official Millennium Prize Problem, still unresolved.
